{{Quote|This place holds much power, both of the light and dark variety.|[[Urai Fen]]|<ref name="FoC">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref>}}
'''Dathomir''' was a remote, obscure and dangerous [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It was inhabited by [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Human/Legends|Humans]] known as the [[Witches of Dathomir]], along with their evil counterparts, the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]]. It was also the homeworld of the dreaded [[Rancor/Legends|rancors]]. Dathomir was the site of numerous battles throughout galactic history.

==Description==
===Geography===
{{Quote|You can't see the stars anywhere on this planet, can you? I mean with the trees and the clouds...|[[Noldan]], to [[Paemos]]|<ref name="SonyCite-Friday Feature – Village of Aurilia">{{SonyCite|url=content.jsp?page=Friday%20Feature%20Village%20of%20Aurilia|text=Friday Feature – Village of Aurilia}}</ref>}}
Dathomir was the fourth planet of [[Dathomir system/Legends|Dathomir system]],<ref name="GatORW" /> located in the [[Quelii sector/Legends|Quelii sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="CTD" /> It had four moons,<ref name="GatORW" /> including [[Koratas]].<ref name="CTD" />

[[File:Dathomir-SWGconcept.jpg|thumb|left|220px|The landscape of Dathomir]]
It was somewhat smaller than [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in size and thus a slightly-below-standard gravity. The planetary day was close to standard though the planetary year was 491 days.<ref name="CTD" />

Dathomir was considered a temperate and beautiful planet by [[Human/Legends|Human]] standards, with a varied terrain that included coastal lakes and tar-pits, thick forests and snow-capped mountain peaks, powerful rivers and broad savannas, small icecaps and dramatic rift valleys. Even under the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], however, nine-tenths of the planet remained unexplored and uninhabited, with the population limited to a relatively small area along the edge of one of the three main continents, a zone of uplands and river plains bordered on one side by the unsailed ocean and on the other by vast expanses of desert.

===Native lifeforms===
{{Quote|In my grandmother's day, we pushed the wild rancors from these mountains. My grandmothers hunted the last of them. We hoped for peace at last.|[[Teneniel Djo]], to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="TCoPL" />}}
Although the two cultures most closely associated with Dathomir were the ancient spacefaring [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]] and the Human group known as the [[Witches of Dathomir]], it should not be overlooked that the [[Sentience/Legends|semi-sentient]] species at the apex of Dathomir's native food-chain was in fact the mighty [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]].

[[File:Rancor_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A rancor.]]
The fact that the rancors were semi-sentient often came as a surprise to unsuspecting offworlders. It is not clear whether they had made any independent progress towards basic tokens of civilization like kindled fire or shaped tools, and their social system and lifestyle were little different from those of many nonsentient animals: matriarchal herds led by [[herd-mother]]s roamed the landscape, hunting live prey for food. But they passed on their clan histories from generation to generation, and when they formed a symbiont circle with the planet's Human population in the last centuries of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], they adopted basic armor and weapons. Under the New Republic, [[Tosh (rancor)|Tosh]], herd-mother of the rancor group, associated with the Human [[Singing Mountain Clan]], learned to read and write, and began to pass on this skill to the other rancors of her herd.

Dathomiri rancors were also larger than off-world specimens, with full-grown adults in the range of eight to ten meters tall. This extreme size can in part be attributed to the planet's low gravity, which allowed native trees to rise up to eighty meters tall, but it may also reflect a more general effect of the sheer vibrancy of the planet's biosphere. The temperate climate and varied terrain had given rise to a dramatically diverse ecosystem, thriving with so much life that the air almost seemed to sparkle in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Other native fauna included the rancor's major prey species, the [[drebbin]] and [[Ssurian/Legends|ssurians]], as well as the [[Burra fish/Legends|burra fish]], the simian pack-hunting [[purbole]] and the acid-jawed, insectile [[shear mite]].

However, several of Dathomir's most important species, notably Humans, had arrived on Dathomir over the millennia as the result of off-world contacts.<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
===Pre-Republic History===
{{Quote|Attuned to the Power of the Cosmos, my people traveled the galaxy via Infinity Gates—portals that transported us instantly between great distances. We observed many worlds and brought civilization to their people.|[[A'nang]]|<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 3">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 3|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 3]]</ref>}}
[[File:Kwa-SW1998-24.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]] built a brilliant civilization in Dathomir ancient times.]]
Dathomir was originally the homeworld of a spacefaring species, the reptilian Kwa.<ref name="TEA" /> By [[100,000 BBY/Legends|100,000 BBY]], the Kwa had built an [[Infinity Gate]]—the [[Prime Gate]] in a network of similar devices, used by them as a means of interstellar travel and as [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]]. The Infinity Gate was covered by massive pyramid-shaped structures known as the [[Star Temple]]s, incorporating defensive systems to protect them from intruders. If the gate was ever activated, the planet housing the equipment could be collapsed into the Gate itself, along with the surrounding planets, moons and even suns.<ref name="FF139">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 139|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 139]]</ref>

For reasons that are unclear, the Kwa species began to degenerate, ultimately losing the ability to speak or use technological tools. Apparently recognizing the path that their civilization was on, they sealed the Infinity Gate and the Star Temples and set guardians to protect the Temples—[[whuffa worm]]s with thick hides and an impressive turn of speed. The degenerate descendants of the Kwa came to be known as the [[Kwi]] or [[Blue Desert People]], and like the rancors they appeared to be simple herd animals living around the planet's arid [[Great Desert of Dathomir|Great Desert]]; but on occasion they still showed some surprising hints of intelligence, including a capability to create primitive tools and ornaments, and they possessed a collective memory of their former glory, and the importance of the sanctity of the Star Temples.<ref name="FF139" />

[[File:Dathomir_Tho_Yor.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The [[Tho Yor Arrival]] on Dathomir.]]
By [[36,453 BBY]], the planet was already inhabited by a few Humans, whose origin is unknown. They were organized in tribal units with [[Shaman/Legends|shamanistic]] beliefs. Some of their seers were [[Tho Yor Arrival|brought]] on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] in a [[Tho Yor]] ship and were among the founders of the [[Je'daii Order]].<ref name="DOJ1">[[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 1|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm'' 1]]</ref>

Around [[30,000 BBY]], Dathomir was ruled by the space-faring [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]]. Using [[Force-drive|Force-based hyperdrives]], they traveled to many worlds around the galaxy that possessed significant signatures in the Force, uniting them to form the Rakatan [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]]. Of Dathomir they noted the rancor, and transferred some of them to their homeworld, [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]], as curiosities. After five thousand years of galactic dominance, the Rakata retreated to Lehon following the outbreak of a [[Rakatan plague|plague]].<ref name="TEA" />

===Old Republic era===
{{Quote|Your people cast them out of the sky for their crimes, and sent them here. The warriors were given no weapons, no metal, no blasters. So they fell prey to rancors. For many generations they lived like beasts, and were nearly hunted to extinction, until the star people cast out Allya.|[[Augwynne Djo]], to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="TCoPL" />}}
Dathomir was the site of a [[Battle of Dathomir (Great Galactic War)|battle]] during the [[Great Galactic War]], a major galactic conflict that opposed the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]].<ref name="The Setting">{{TORweb|url=info/story/setting|text=Game Setting|nolive=1}}</ref>

Around [[3000 BBY]], Dathomir became an adjunct of an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] empire known as the [[Paecian Empire]].<ref name="TEA" /> The [[Paecia/Legends|Paecians]] established a stable population on the planet.<ref name="BoS" /> The later Human populations of Dathomir mostly derived from those Paecian settlers and the [[Paecian/Legends|Paecian]] language was still spoken on Dathomir thousands years after the collapse of the Paecian Empire.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Dathomirtcw.png|thumb|right|250px|A surface on Dathomir]]
After the disappearance of the Paecian Empire, Dathomir fell under the control of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] who also settled the world for some times.<ref name="BoS" /> Around [[1002 BBY]], during the [[New Sith Wars]], the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] operated a [[Sith Academy (Dathomir)|Sith academy]] on the world that trained [[Sith acolyte/Legends|Sith Acolytes]] and [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentices]].<ref name="DB:PoD" /> These Sith later abandoned the planet.<ref name="BoS" />

During the last centuries of the Galactic Republic, the planet was used as a penal colony by the Republic. Some of its worst criminals were sent to Dathomir where they were forced to spend the rest of their life struggling against the world's hostile fauna.<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> Without weapons or technology, they had become little more than the favorite food for the rancors who exterminated them. Later Dathomiri tradition would remember this exiled criminals as a group of creators of illegal and dangerous [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]].<ref name="TCoPL" />

===The Daughters of Allya===
{{Quote|We tried to free the Chu'unthor from Dathomir, but were repulsed by the witches.|[[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="TCoPL" />}}
[[File:Singing_Mountain_Sister.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A [[Singing Mountain Clan]] sister riding a rancor.]]
In [[600 BBY/Legends|600 BBY]], a rogue [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] named [[Allya/Legends|Allya]] was banished to Dathomir by the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]]. She took the leadership of the survivors, teaching the ways of the Force to the exiles, and eventually to her own children. In later centuries, Allya was remembered as single-handedly transforming Dathomiri society, credited with enslaving the entire male population under her leadership, turning the rancors from predators to friends, pets, and war mounts, and codifying her teachings in the [[Book of Law/Legends|Book of Law]]. Some accounts even seem to suppose that she was a lone woman within an otherwise entirely male population. But in reality, these practices may have evolved over several generations, and the parallel with the matriarchal social structure of the rancors may be significant, especially given the symbiosis of the Human warrior-women and their mounts; but Allya's leadership undoubtedly laid the foundations of a unique culture, dominated by Force-using women who regarded themselves collectively as her descendants, known to outsiders as the Witches of Dathomir.

[[File:Nightsister_Patrol_Leader.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]].]]
Over the centuries, the total Human population of Dathomir grew to perhaps just over five thousand, based in a relatively narrow coastal area of one of the planet's continents: even under the New Republic, more than 90% of the planet remained unexplored. The Dathomiri came to be divided into a number of reasonably permanent local clan communities, which took their names from significant geographical features such as [[Singing Mountain (Dathomir)/Legends|Singing Mountain]], [[Frenzied River]], and [[Misty Falls/Legends|Misty Falls]]. These clans, each just a few hundred strong, accounted for almost the entire planetary population, but there were also small numbers of exiles who lived outside the clan communities, including the planet's dark-siders, called [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]], who at times existed in sufficient numbers to form a distinct clan. In total, the clans could probably put at least a thousand warrior-women into the field, each of them a trained Force-user and many of them riding rancor mounts.

The strength of the Dathomiri was discovered by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in around [[340 BBY]],<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> when the [[Jedi academy]] ship ''[[Chu'unthor]]'' crashed into a tar pit on Dathomir. The [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], [[Gra'aton]] and [[Vulatan]] then traveled to the planet but all attempts to retrieve the wreck were blocked by the natives. Centuries later, the witches still remembered, albeit in a embellished way, the day when they defeated the powerful [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]].<ref name="TCoPL" /> Sometimes later, Yoda returned to Dathomir and negotiated a peaceful settlement of this affair.<ref name="TNEC" /> One young warrior-woman, [[Rell (Dathomir)|Rell]], who would survive over centuries to meet [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] in the days of the New Republic, reminisced about Yoda as an "old flirt".<ref name="TCoPL" /> Nevertheless, the wreckage of the ''Chu'unthor'' remained on the planet. Following this incident, the Jedi Council interdicted access to the planet.<ref name="GatORW" />

[[File:DaughtersOfDathomir-TSWB.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian Zabrak-Human hybrids]].]]
Generations prior to the Clone Wars, a small group of [[Iridonian (species)|Iridonian]] [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabraks]] originating from [[Rattatak/Legends|Rattatak]], where their ancestors had crashed in a [[Starship/Legends|starcruiser]], were brought to Dathomir during [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] raids. When the Human Nightsisters discovered that they could interbreed with Zabraks, they isolated them to a small part of the planet where they could draw from them at whim. The Nightsisters also sold some Zabraks and [[Dathomirian/Legends|Zabrak-Human hybrids]] (and even some of their own) to the [[Rattataki/Legends|Rattataki]].<ref name="EYAWtKAtNbWAtA" /> Prior to the reign of [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]], Nightsisters were known to utilize various male castaways for slave labor;<ref name="Infinity" /> Talzin restricted the use of males to the Zabrak [[Nightbrothers/Legends|Nightbrothers]].

===Later History===
{{Quote|You presume to assault us on our home planet? You will pay for your arrogance!|Nightsister to two Jedi sent to Dathomir|<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance]]''</ref>}}
[[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] visited Dathomir in [[54 BBY/Legends|54 BBY]] and was approached by the Nightsister [[Kycina]], who begged him to take away her infant son from the life of a Nightbrother. Sidious agreed, taking in the Zabrak who would soon become his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], the fearsome [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]].<ref name="DP" />

[[File:StarTemple-SWREP23.jpg|thumb|right|180px|[[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] approaching a [[Star Temple]].]]
In [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]], many Kwi were decimated by a clan of Nightsisters during their attempt to access the secrets of the Infinity Gate. [[Zalem/Legends|Zalem]], styling herself as the Queen of the Nightsisters, intended to use the device to destroy Coruscant. Their plot was [[Mission to Dathomir (Post–Naboo crisis)|thwarted]] by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]], who was able to make contact with the Kwa, and assumed the role of Temple Guardian, to redirect the deadly [[Infinity Wave]] aimed at Coruscant back at the Infinity Gate. Only the scattered ruins of the Infinity Gate and the Star Temple were left, and the Kwi disappeared once more to roam the deserts.<ref name="Infinity" /> As Coruscant was almost destroyed by the Kwa superweapon, the Jedi later deleted all references to Dathomir from all available records.<ref name="GatORW" />

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] led an [[Battle of Dathomir/Legends|attack]] on the Nightsisters, in retaliation for the betrayal of [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] and Mother Talzin. This assault led to the extermination of almost every [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian]] Nightsister,<ref name="Massacre" /> and thus resulting in the original Human Nightsisters<ref name="EYAWtKAtNbWAtA" /> eventually returning to prominence on Dathomir.<ref name="TCoPL" /><ref name="SWG" />

[[File:Droids-Second-Battle-of-Dathomir.png|thumb|left|200px|[[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] droids invading Dathomir.]]
In the waning hours of the Clone Wars the planet would be successfully invaded once again by a Separatist contingent led by Darth Sidious himself along with the cyborg General Grievous. They were on a mission to destroy Mother Talzin once and for all, who had taken possession of [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] body after being captured by Darth Maul. Upon Mother Talzin's death at the hands of Grievous, the planet was taken over by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] presumably until the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|galactic conflict]].<ref name="DDMSoD" />

Prior to the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Dathomir was conquered by [[Drackmarian]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]].<ref name="TEA" /> However, this planet held little real interest for these methane-breathing aliens. Prior to the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Dathomir was owned by the female Drackmarian warlord [[Omogg]].<ref name="TCoPL" />

===Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|The planet's name is Dathomir. It seems the planet holds many Force users of great power. However, the Emperor found it first - he's blockaded the planet and placed a nightcloak generator system in orbit.|[[Urai Fen]]|<ref name="FoC" />}}
After the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], the fabled village of [[Aurilia]] was believed to be located somewhere on Dathomir, and it was rumored that [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] individuals, perhaps even Jedi, lived here in exile during the reign of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="SWG" />

Around the time of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] [[Passenger liner/Legends|passenger liner]] ''[[Tzarina]]'' crashed on Dathomir, causing the death of most passengers.<ref name="SWG:ac">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=herald|a commoner|Dathomir}}</ref>

[[File:dathprison.jpg|thumb|right|230px|The [[Dathomir Imperial Prison]].]]
Also around the time of the Battle of Yavin, the Galactic Empire established a [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] on the Dathomir,<ref name="GatORW" /> with the objective to re-establish the old penal colony.<ref name="TDSS" /> While [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] was aware of the presence of the witches, he allowed the construction of a [[Dathomir Imperial Prison|prison]] on the planet.<ref name="GatORW" /> Imperial troops initially encountered no resistance from the Witches,<ref name="Insider">{{InsiderCite|65|Who's Who in Star Wars Galaxies|Who's Who in ''Star Wars'' Galaxies}}</ref> and focused their efforts in hunting the remaining Kwi to near-extinction.<ref name="GatORW" />

Shortly after the Imperials arrived, an exile from the Singing Mountain Clan named [[Gethzerion]] and her clan of Nightsisters approached the Imperial [[Commander/Legends|commander]] and offered their services to control prisoners. Although the commander was suspicious about her true intentions, he accepted the offer. Gethzerion and her dark minions thus became a familiar sight in the Imperial compound.<ref name="TDSS" /> Using the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], the Nightsisters soon began to [[Mind trick/Legends#Force corrupt|corrupt]] the Imperial troops and progressively usurped control of the prison. When the Empire discovered the situation, Gethzerion and the Nightsisters turned Imperial troops against their officers. A [[Invasion of Dathomir|battle]] therefore erupted on Dathomir between loyal Imperial forces and the Nightsisters backed by their Imperial [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]]. Eventually, the Nightsisters were defeated and repelled from the prison.<ref name="Insider" />

[[File:OrbitalNightcloakOrbit-FF35.png|thumb|left|250px|Some of the orbital nightcloaks above Dathomir.]]
When Palpatine realized the threat Gethzerion and the Nightsisters posed in the Force, he quickly placed the planet under strict [[Blockade of Dathomir|interdiction]].<ref name="TDSS" /> Shortly after the Battle of Yavin, [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Zsinj]] [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombarded]] the Imperial prison from [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]], destroying every vessels parked there to prevent the Nightsisters to leave Dathomir.<ref name="TNEGtC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Imperial ships were stationed in the system to prevent further contact with the surface and to perform orbital scans periodically to ensure that the Nightsisters were still confined, with strict orders to never land on the planet.<ref name="TDSS" /> The Emperor ordered that at least two [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] guarded the planet at all times.<ref name="CTD" /> Additionally, [[orbital nightcloak]]s were deployed in orbit.<ref name="FoC" /> The prison and all Imperial forces at the surface were abandoned.<ref name="GatORW" /> These troops continued to fight the Nightsisters for years,<ref name="Insider" /> but Gethzerion and her clan eventually enslaved the stranded Imperial garrison.<ref name="GatORW" /> For his role in the containment of Dathomir, Captain Zsinj was promoted to [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] by the Emperor and was given command of the new [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] [[Iron Fist (Executor-class)|''Iron Fist'']].<ref name="TNEGtC" /> In the next years, Zsinj became [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] of the [[Quelii Oversector]]<ref name="TEGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and continued to oversee the blockade of Dathomir.<ref name="CTD" /> Commanding the largest fleet of the Empire, Zsinj later defeated the Drackmarians.<ref name="TEGtW" />.

[[File:NammanCha-TNR.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Namman Cha]] observes a Nightsister on her rancor mount.]]
Despite the presence of the Imperial blockade, the Dathomir system attracted a great deal of attention at the height of the Galactic Civil War, being the site of numerous skirmishes between Imperial and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] forces.<ref name="Sony">{{SonyCite|url=expansions_sectors_dath.jsp|text=Dathomir System}}</ref> By [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{StarWarsGalaxiesDate}}</ref> the blockade had been quite loosened, being focused in one [[Empire Blockade|quadrant]] of Dathomir space. Intrepid [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] frequently managed to lure the Imperial [[Dathomir Station]] and get through the blockade to land at one of the two outposts present on Dathomir: the [[Trade Outpost]] and the [[Science Outpost]].<ref name="SWG" /> One year after the Battle of Yavin,<ref name="SWG_timeline" /> the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Mellichae]] discovered the secret village of Aurilia but his [[Sith Shadows]] minions were defeated in battle by a group of Force-sensitive spacers.<ref name="SWG" />

In addition, the Empire had established on the planet a secret [[Imperial Research and Prison Facility]] where scientists studied the dangerous [[Imperial bioweapons Project I71A|Blackwing Virus]].<ref name="SWG:GU14">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=other|Game Update 14: Death Troopers}}</ref> In 1 ABY,<ref name="SWG_timeline" /> an [[Blackwing virus outbreak on Dathomir|outbreak]] of the Blackwing Virus happened following an accident in the Imperial Research and Prison Facility. A large area of land was [[Quarantine Zone (Dathomir)|quarantined]] by Imperial troops and was directly supervised by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. Groups of spacers where eventually permitted entrance, and did several quest to keep people safe and defeat [[Zombie/Legends|zombies]].<ref name="SWG:GU14" /> During this period, a group of mercenaries known as the [[Witchblood Clan]] was active in Dathomir space. They usually attacked both Rebels and Imperials indiscriminately.<ref name="Sony" />

[[File:Quarantine_Zone_zombies_2.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Zombie/Legends|Undeads]] in the [[Quarantine Zone (Dathomir)|Quarantine Zone]] of Dathomir.]]

Around this time, [[Tyber Zann]] and [[Urai Fen]] of the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]] [[Ground Battle on Dathomir|arrived]] on the planet, seeking one who could unlock a [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocron]] in Tyber's possession. They found an imprisoned Nightsister, [[Silri]], capable of doing so, and freed her, from an Imperial prison. After helping her to kill the [[Unidentified Imperial governor (Dathomir)|Imperial governor of Dathomir]], Tyber Zann recruited Silri and a group of Nightsisters to his service.<ref name="FoC" />

After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] Zsinj refused to recognize the authority of the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]] and declared himself a Warlord, quickly coming to rival the power of both the legitimist Imperial authorities and the rising New Republic. Dathomir became key to his plans with the discovery of vast loads of the key shipbuilding metals of [[Neutronium/Legends|neutronium]], [[Lommite/Legends|lommite]], and [[Zersium/Legends|zersium]] on the moon [[Koratas]], and Zsinj had the [[Rancor Base]] [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]] built in orbit of the planet to exploit the world's resources. All Zsinj's shipbuilding facilities were moved to the Dathomir system that became his secretly headquarters.<ref name="CTD" />

===New Republic===
{{Quote|There are a lot of Force-sensitives in the population, most of whom are trained in the so-called Witchcraft of Dathomir. There's not a lot of government oversight.|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], to [[Ben Skywalker]]|<ref name="Backlash" />}}
[[File:IsolderRancor.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Teneniel Djo]] and [[Isolder]] riding rancors through the Dathomir jungle.]]
A few years after the Battle of Endor, General [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] was commanding the New Republic [[Hunt for Zsinj|campaign]] against Imperial Warlord Zsinj.<ref name="TCoPL" /> In the meantime, the Drackmarians discovered that Zsinj's base was located above Dathomir. They then elaborated a subtle move to attract the New Republic to Dathomir.<ref name="TEGtW" /> Hence, Han Solo won the deed to Dathomir from Drackmarian Warlord Omogg in a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] in [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], unaware that the planet was in fact controlled by Zsinj. Han's kidnapping of [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] to the planet led to a chain of events that changed Dathomir forever. Luke Skywalker and Prince [[Isolder]], the heir of the [[Hapes Consortium/Legends|Hapes Consortium]], followed Solo and Organa to Dathomir and encountered the witches of the Singing Mountain Clan but also Gethzerion and her Nightsisters. The following [[Battle of Dathomir (Hunt for Zsinj)|battle]] resulted in the destruction of the Nightsisters and [[Zsinj's Empire]]. A large [[Hapan Royal Navy|Hapan fleet]] sent by [[Ta'a Chume]], the [[Queen Mother]] of the Hapes Consortium suddenly attacked Zsinj's fleet, destroying most of the fleet, including the ''Iron Fist'', as well as Rancor Base and the orbital nightcloaks. Both Zsinj and Gethzerion were killed in the battle.<ref name="TCoPL" /> The Imperial blockade was definitively broken as all remaining Imperial forces quickly fled the system.<ref name="CTD" /> The prisoners of the Imperial prison, mostly political prisoners, were also liberated.<ref name="TCoPL" />

[[File:BattleofDathomir.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The [[Battle of Dathomir (Hunt for Zsinj)|Battle of Dathomir]].]]
After the death of Zsinj, Han Solo gave over his claim to the planet to [[Augwynne Djo]], matriarch of the Singing Mountain Clan.<ref name="TCoPL" /> The woman was soon able to unite Dathomiri clans and requested membership into the New Republic.<ref name="CTD" /> Augwynne's new title as planetary leader of Dathomir was little more than a constitutional formality bit it also ennobled her granddaughter [[Teneniel Djo]], and enabled her to marry Isolder, with whom she had fallen in love.<ref name="TCoPL" /> Free from the tyranny of the Empire, the planet was later integrated into the New Republic.<ref name="TEA" /> Moreover, the Dathomiri witch Teneniel Djo became the queen of the Hapes Consortium after her wedding, thereby becoming the leader of a rich and powerful interstellar government ruling 63 inhabited worlds.<ref name="CTD" />

Several witches of Dathomir subsequently went on to train with Luke Skywalker after he funded his [[Jedi Praxeum]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]],<ref name="JvS" /> including [[Kirana Ti]] and [[Damaya]].<ref name="TUF">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref>

In [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], the forces of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] returned to Dathomir, in the form of an expedition searching for the Infinity Gate, led by [[Sigit Ranth]] and [[General/Legends|General]] [[Vit]]. The Imperials overpowered the small [[New Republic embassy (Dathomir)|New Republic embassy]] on the planet, and struck an alliance with a group of Dathomiri who styled themselves as a reborn clan of Nightsisters. Although Ranth soon departed the world when he discovered that the Infinity Gate was inoperable, General Vit and his garrison remained, tasked with imposing Imperial authority on Dathomir in alliance with the Nightsisters, investigating the Jedi artifacts on the ''Chu'unthor'', and recruiting the planet's Force-sensitive warriors for the service of the Empire. Over the next months, Vit and his men reconditioned the old Imperial prison facility, and began rounding up the hostile Dathomiri and incarcerating them. Soon, the Singing Mountain Clan had been imprisoned in the camp, and prison columns from the defeated [[Dreaming River Clan]] were being marched under guard to join them. At this point, a miscellaneous group of heroes and rogues arrived on the planet, including renegade [[Special forces/Legends|special forces]] officer and Jedi Praxeum trainee [[Dal Konur]], as well as Imperial [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guard]] [[Kir Kanos]]. Working together with the Dathomiri resistance, they succeeded in ousting Vit and the Imperials; but neither the Empire nor the Nightsisters had been permanently destroyed.<ref name="Nightsaber" />

[[File:DathomirFlag.png|thumb|right|200px|Flag of Dathomir]]
In [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]],<ref name="GatORW" /> the Dark Jedi [[Brakiss]] arrived on Dathomir. A Force-sensitive [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] agent working with the faction known as the [[Second Imperium]], he infiltrated the [[Great Canyon Clan]] and transformed them into a new group of Nightsisters, to serve as a recruiting pool for the [[Shadow Academy]]. Brakiss also engineered a social revolution, so that the new Nightsisters came to treat males as equals—adding escaped slaves from the other clans to their ranks. By [[23 ABY/Legends|23 ABY]], some Great Canyon Clan warriors, like [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Garowyn]], had already undergone thorough training at the Shadow Academy, and received commissions in the Imperial military. Later that year, however, [[Tenel Ka Djo|Tenel Ka]] and Skywalker infiltrated the Great Canyon and from there were able to reach the Shadow Academy.<ref name="SA">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Shadow Academy]]''</ref> The clan's strength would be subsequently slashed by their [[Third Battle of Yavin|defeat]] in the Second Imperium's attack on Yavin 4.<ref name="JUS">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Jedi Under Siege]]''</ref>

===Galactic Alliance===
{{Quote|There's no world better suited to be the home of this new Sith Order than Dathomir.|Luke Skywalker, to Ben Skywalker|<ref name="Backlash" />}}
During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Dathomir was an obvious target for the extra-galactic invaders in their crusade against the Jedi and other [[Force Adept]]s.<ref name="TEA" /> As the planet lacked technology and planetary defenses, it was easily [[Invasion of Dathomir (Yuuzhan Vong War)|invaded]] by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]. However, the invaders soon realized that the native Witches of Dathomir were going to be harder to subdue. Despite long months of fighting, Dathomir was never fully conquered.<ref name="GatORW" /> Unable to defeat the Witches through conventional ground assaults, the Yuuzhan Vong renounced to their objective to control the planet and eventually left the star system.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:WitchBattle-TSS.png|thumb|left|220px|A Dathomir Witch defends herself against a Nightsister.]]
After the war's end, Jedi Master [[Streen]], with the help of Dathomiri Jedi Kirana Ti, did a great deal of work on the ravaged Dathomir and founded a [[Jedi Praxeum (Dathomir)|Praxeum]] in order to train the local witches as Jedi.<ref name="JvS" /> At some point, a [[Dathomir Spaceport|spaceport]] was established on the planet by the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]].<ref name="Backlash" />

In the following years, [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] came to the planet and trained in the arts of the indigenous witches.<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref> Later, in [[43 ABY]], just prior to the [[Lost Tribe of Sith emergence]], Skywalker and his son [[Ben Skywalker|Ben]] tracked [[Vestara Khai]] to the planet and were re-joined by Han, Leia, and [[Allana Djo Solo|Allana Solo]]. The Jedi became [[Conclave of the Raining Leaves Clan and the Broken Columns Clan|involved]] in some [[Duel in the Dathomir landing meadow|affairs]] on the world, including a resurgent clan of Nightsisters and a proposed Sith-Nightsister alliance.<ref name="Backlash" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Frenzied_River_region.png|thumb|right|250px|A map of Dathomir.]]
The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] places Dathomir in the "Quelli sector", a misspelling of the true Quelii Sector.

According to ''Cracken's Threat Dossier'', Dathomir was admitted to the Hapan worlds, this despite the significant distance separating the two.

A character in ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' stated that Dathomir was located in the [[Quelii system/Legends|Quelii system]], but with the release of ''[[Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed]]'', the system you travel to when traveling to Dathomir is called the [[Dathomir system/Legends|Dathomir system]]. The game still presents these two conflicting pieces of information.
